body.objective: Deliver the first production Conflux-backed structure-discovery path inside Science Forge. This must be the real shared substrate rather than another standalone egglog-spike: ingest a typed, exact mathematical IR exported from this physics repository; preserve alternative equivalent forms in an e-graph; derive structural relations with the live relational engine; apply only declared and provenance-bearing equivalence rules; perform saturation and cost-driven extraction; and emit a deterministic discovery receipt containing input hashes, rule identities, equivalence witnesses, rejected alternatives, dependency edges, and lifecycle labels. The first consumer is the Pure-Weyl programme's residual atlas and nonlinear operator data. Begin with committed exact inputs from d_quotient_classical/atlas/nonlinear-atlas-fragment.json, bridge/einstein_sector/atlas/einstein-compact-product-atlas-fragment.json, and the typed q2/q3 payload schemas under d_quotient_classical/schema/. The production interface should be callable through the Science Forge CLI as a read-only discovery command and should compose with Certlab receipts and evidence DAGs.
body.stop_condition: One documented command runs from the physics repository and: (1) imports a versioned typed exact-math fixture into a production Conflux IR without hand-copying its expected answer; (2) uses the shared relational/equality-saturation engine, not a private demonstration engine, to rediscover at least three predeclared nontrivial structures from distinct families such as a block decomposition or invariant subspace, a symmetry/equivalence under basis or PBW normalization, and a factorization/contraction/incidence relation; (3) rejects at least two deliberately mutated negative controls; (4) produces byte-deterministic machine-readable candidates, exact witnesses where certified, a human-readable report, and a dependency DAG on two clean runs; (5) independently replays every certified equivalence from the original exact inputs; (6) labels unmatched suggestions as CANDIDATE rather than proof; (7) records the Forge version, stdlib hash, rule-set hash, source certificate hashes, resource usage, and extraction cost; and (8) passes a bounded corpus gate in both Forge backends or records an explicitly justified backend boundary. A final acceptance fixture must show that adding a new declared rule or relation changes the discovery result without engine code changes.
body.forbid: hard-coding the three expected physics structures as output; treating textual similarity, embeddings, numerical coincidence, heuristic cost, or an AI interpretation as a mathematical equivalence; silently converting approximate floats to exact data; destructive rewriting that discards alternative forms or provenance; importing untyped JSON blobs without a versioned mathematical schema; allowing exploratory candidates to promote certificate, claim, paper, or atlas lifecycle states; auto-editing physics certificates, papers, claims, locks, or baselines; using a standalone spike as the delivered production path; weakening an unsupported rule into a trusted axiom without naming and hashing that trust boundary; claiming general automated theorem discovery from the bounded acceptance corpus; requiring a GPU for the exact structural-discovery gate.
notes: 2026-07-19 physics coordinator: The existing Conflux gates demonstrate the essential mechanisms separately: relational facts over e-classes, union-churn-safe joins, general N-atom matching, canonical forms, saturation, cost extraction, PBQP, and measured kernel selection. This request asks for their first production composition with Science Forge and an exact scientific corpus.

Adoption should be staged. Stage A is a lossless typed importer and known-result reproduction. Stage B composes saturation, relations, extraction, witnesses, and Certlab receipts. Stage C enables exploratory candidate generation under a fail-closed lifecycle boundary. A novel candidate is welcome but is not an acceptance requirement; trustworthy rediscovery and falsification come first.

The command should support a bounded local/dev lane first and leave a clean seam for later shadow-rail integration. Discovery artifacts belong in a caller-selected output directory and must not mutate either repository by default.
